catalog_quote: [p. 285, table row] a 1 | CV̀, CV̀C | CV̀V̀, CV̀CV̀, CV̀CV̀CV̀ | 'bozom ... Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). [p. 345] Remarque. On pourrait poser que la langue ancestrale ne connaissait que des syllabes ouvertes et un accent : *CV, *CVCV (qui aurait donné CVCV non accentué) et *CVCV (qui aurait donné CVC). L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution.

new_statements.translation: [p. 285] Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them at present shows any phenomenon of accent, of intensity [stress] or of length. The hypothesis will be raised again diachronically, when the sound correspondences are interpreted (p. 345). [p. 345] Remark. One could posit that the ancestral language had only open syllables and an accent ... The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not impose this solution for Proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis can be entertained for an earlier stage.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Gbaya 'bozom, like all 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka varieties Moñino surveyed first-hand, is a tone language (two level tones in the western area, 'bozom drifting toward a third level per pp. 152-157) with no accent: the author explicitly denies any present-day phenomenon of accent, intensity (stress) or length, and treats accent only as a speculative pre-Proto-Gbaya reconstruction.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None (no stress of any kind per source).
new_statements.exceptions: None. The only qualification is diachronic: an accent is entertained as a hypothesis for a pre-Proto-Gbaya stage to explain CVCV vs CVC reflexes, explicitly not for the modern languages.
new_statements.domain_note: Blanket synchronic statement in the contrastive summary of tonal morphophonology (the 'modificateur relationnel'), covering every language in the study; 'bozom is named in the table row (area a1) that the remark comments on, and Moñino's 'bozom data are his own (900-item list, 200 sentences, a recorded tale; informants from Gbadare 2, 1970-73, pp. 51-52). Word/lexical prosody is meant (accent vs. lexical/grammatical tone); the dedicated 'bozom chapter (pp. 142-158) could not be opened to check for a chapter-internal restatement.
new_statements.identity_note: Moñino's 'gbaya 'bozom' = the Gbaya spoken around Bozoum (clans calling themselves bòkòtò, mbaï, all 'bozôm', p. 142 snippet), i.e. Glottolog Gbaya-Bozoum gbay1286 [gbq], dialect Bozom [bozo1251]; Glottolog's own language code mapping for this reference reads 'Gbaya Bozom = Gbaya-Bozoum [gbq]'. His data come from the village Gbadare 2. The quoted sentence is a blanket statement over all 21 varieties in the study (it is not inside the 'bozom chapter), but 'bozom is explicitly one of the languages in the table the remark comments on. The closest sister variety, Gbeya/Gbaya-Bossangoa (gbay1287, gbp), is already in the catalog as no word stress from Ruckstuhl 1998/2007 and Samarin 1966, consistent with this finding; do not merge the two keys.

What is held by the project of the chapter is only Google search-within-volume snippets : p. 142 'Le gbayá bòzôm est parlé dans la région de Bozoum par plusieurs clans dont les uns se disent bòkòtò, d'autres mbaï, et tous bozôm'; p. 152 'bozom s'orienterait alors vers une structure à trois tons ponctuels pertinents lexicaux et grammaticaux, et aurait par là un caractère unique dans le groupe gbaya-manza-ngbaka'; p. 157 'bozom est un laboratoire vivant.. on y assiste à la complication de la structure tonale, au passage d'un état binaire à un état encore confus qui paraît pouvoir aboutir à la créa…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Gbaya 'bozom is a tone language (two lexical/grammatical tones drifting toward a three-tone system, pp. 152-157 per snippets) with no word stress: Moñino states that none of the 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka languages surveyed, 'bozom explicitly among them (area a1 of the table the remark annotates), shows any accent, intensity or length phenomenon; the syllable-type-conditioned tone sandhi is not accent-driven. A pre-proto-Gbaya accent is entertained only as a diachronic hypothesis.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (no stress at all per the source).
new_statements.exceptions: None. The only qualification is diachronic: p. 345 allows that an earlier stage than proto-Gbaya might have had an accent (*CVCV with accent giving CVC), while stating that the present-day languages have no accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Moñino's 'bozom = gbayá bòzôm spoken around Bozoum (CAR) by clans calling themselves bòkòtò or mbaï and all bozôm (p. 142 snippet); his informants were 'Bozom of the village Gbadare 2, corpus about 900 terms (pp. 51-52). Glottolog gbay1286 'Gbaya-Bozoum' [gbq] names this variety; Moñino's remark on p. 285 is a statement about all languages in his survey, with 'bozom explicitly the sole member of tonal area a1 in the annotated table, so it applies to this variety and not only to the Gbaya group in general.
